# Managed merchant package installation

Install a maintained `@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant` package into the
original SF46 versioned home. Each release keeps the package's original
`source/` tree, `package.json`, `manifest.json`, README and license. The existing
installer supplies staging, active and previous release selection, a stable
`forge.mjs` entry point, and separate merchant configuration and state.

Use Node 22.16 or later and a local filesystem on one host. The original
installation uses atomic rename and hard links for its update records.

## Select the package directory

The input is the directory containing the maintained package's `package.json`,
`manifest.json` and `source/`. For an existing local npm installation this is
`node_modules/@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant`. A `.tgz` delivery can also be
extracted into a new directory using the host's ordinary archive tools; npm
archives contain that same directory under `package/`.

The installed command is:

```sh
npx --no-install starforge installation --help
```

From a current source checkout, the same command can run directly. This also
allows a retained earlier package to enter the managed installation:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf46-release/package-cli.mjs --help
```

The examples below use the installed alias. Substitute the direct Node command
when working from source. Choose absolute paths for the package and private home:

```sh
STARFORGE_PACKAGE_DIR=/absolute/path/to/package
STARFORGE_INSTALLATION=/absolute/private/starforge

npx --no-install starforge installation inspect "$STARFORGE_PACKAGE_DIR"
```

Inspection reports the original package name and version, source commit,
`sourceManifestSha256`, source count and bytes, mapped native commands, runtime
declarations and separate dependency entries. Every original manifest entry is
checked against its declared bytes, SHA-256 and Git blob identity. Root package
files and their metadata are checked against the same source declarations.

When the delivery supplies its manifest SHA-256, pass that exact value:

```sh
npx --no-install starforge installation inspect "$STARFORGE_PACKAGE_DIR" \
  --expect-manifest PUBLISHED_MANIFEST_SHA256
```

`--expect-manifest` refers to the exact bytes of the package's `manifest.json`.
The archive checksum identifies the `.tgz` file; the prepared SF46 `digest`
identifies the installed release. Each value keeps its own file and purpose.

## Install and reopen the managed home

```sh
npx --no-install starforge installation install "$STARFORGE_PACKAGE_DIR" \
  --home "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION" \
  --expect-manifest PUBLISHED_MANIFEST_SHA256

npx --no-install starforge installation status --home "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION"
```

Omit `--expect-manifest` when inspecting and installing without an externally
supplied manifest comparison. The first installation needs a new or empty home,
outside the original package directory, and becomes active automatically.

The install result includes the original install `state`, `releaseId`, release
`digest`, `activeReleaseId`, `staged`, `releaseDirectory`, configuration and state
paths, plus the package version, source commit and original manifest hash. The
manager prepares a temporary complete release, passes its exact digest to the
original installer, then removes only its own temporary directory.

The stable entry point is stored in the home. It works in a new terminal without
the command's original npm application or source checkout:

```sh
node "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION/forge.mjs" status
```

| Home path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `forge.mjs`, `release-core.mjs` | Original installed manager |
| `installation.json`, `active.json` | Home identity and active/previous release selection |
| `releases/RELEASE_ID/` | Complete versioned package and SF46 release manifest |
| `config/` | Operator configuration retained across code upgrades |
| `state/` | Merchant workspaces, journals and retained operational files |

The installed package still contains its original `package.json` export and bin
paths. Imports beneath `source/` resolve through the same directory structure.
The package's existing `node_modules/` and `package-lock.json`, when present in
the input, remain separate dependency state; prepare copies the original
manifested source into the release.

## Storage during preparation and installation

Preparation copies the original manifest-bound source files into a private
release directory. Each destination has a separate inode, receives the declared
source mode, and is checked against its complete byte count and SHA-256. Node
requests copy-on-write storage where reflinks are supported and otherwise uses
an ordinary copy. The retained original runtime is never consumed, linked for
writing, or modified by this operation.

Runtime adoption then hands its own newly prepared directory to the existing
installer. On the same filesystem, the installer moves that private directory
into its locked installation stage instead of allocating another complete
source copy. It verifies the entire staged release before promotion, prepares
the original runtime attachment, and selects the release only after that
attachment succeeds. Interrupted attachment recovery reuses the same installed
release through the existing adoption workflow.

This transfer applies only to the adopter's private preparation. Ordinary
bundle installation keeps the caller's bundle and uses verified create-only
copies. A cross-filesystem adoption also uses that complete copy path. The
installed release and original runtime retain their ordinary files, and
portable archives remain complete without reflink support. No CLI flag or
additional dependency is required.

Reserve space for the complete fallback copy unless the actual source and
installation placement establishes the same-filesystem transfer. The original
home lock, staging cleanup, attachment and activation order still govern the
operation; the adopter cleans its own temporary parent after success or failure.

## Start the original merchant workspace

The `starforge` native command runs the original toolkit, including its
workspace `init`, `run` and `source` commands. Keep the merchant workspace inside
the home's retained configuration directory:

```sh
node "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION/forge.mjs" run starforge -- init \
  --dir "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION/config/merchant" --template dataset

node "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION/forge.mjs" run starforge -- run \
  --workspace "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION/config/merchant" -- --port 0
```

The original seller and operations launcher print their actual addresses. Open
the operations address for the merchant dashboard. The dataset starter uses the
maintained example configuration; its `/dataset` request returns the original
HTTP 402 challenge until the native payment runtime and merchant terms are
configured. Edit the workspace's existing `seller.json` and dataset through the
normal merchant workflow. Ctrl-C reaches the running command's shutdown path.

The first `--` belongs to the installation manager. The second `--` in the
workspace launch belongs to the original toolkit and forwards seller options.
Arguments keep their original boundaries and the caller's working directory.
Absolute configuration and state paths work across operator terminals.

Every mapped native command remains available directly:

```sh
npx --no-install starforge installation run buyer --home "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION" -- --help
node "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION/forge.mjs" run operations -- --help
node "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION/forge.mjs" run starforge -- source
```

`status.commands` is the exact installed map. `status.commandCatalog` identifies
the maintained catalog and the original SF46 compatibility aliases.

## Stage an upgrade, activate it and roll back

Retain the next supplied package in its own directory, then install it into the
same home:

```sh
npx --no-install starforge installation install /absolute/path/to/next-package \
  --home "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION" \
  --expect-manifest NEXT_PUBLISHED_MANIFEST_SHA256

npx --no-install starforge installation status --home "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION"
```

Later installs are staged. Use the exact `releaseId` returned by that install to
select the new source for subsequent launches:

```sh
npx --no-install starforge installation activate RELEASE_ID --home "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION"
npx --no-install starforge installation rollback --home "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION"
```

`install ... --activate` combines staging and selection. Repeating installation
of the same prepared identity reuses the existing release. The release digest
also records the exact original SF46 manager bytes used for preparation.

Activation changes source for new launches. A running merchant retains its
selected code until the original process exits; use its normal drain/shutdown
flow, then launch through the home again. Merchant configuration, databases and
journals remain in their existing paths throughout activation and rollback.
Data migration and recovery follow the original merchant's own procedures.

The original manager retains the previous release and serializes local update
operations. A competing live update reports its process; continue the intended
update after that operation exits. An interrupted first install resumes with
the same package and the same manager source, preserving its original release
digest. A completed staged release can be selected with `activate` after restart.
Old releases remain available in the home for explicit operator management.

## Optional runtime packages

Run the original installed dependency doctor:

```sh
npx --no-install starforge installation doctor --home "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION"
npx --no-install starforge installation doctor --home "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION" --feature postgres
npx --no-install starforge installation doctor --home "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION" --native
```

The selected release's maintained doctor reports actual local imports and
runtime availability. A requested missing feature or native runtime returns its
original failing exit status. The package retains its declared optional
dependency versions and peer ranges.

For a source-only managed release, use the original package setup in the exact
`releaseDirectory` returned by install or status:

```sh
cd /absolute/private/starforge/releases/ACTUAL_RELEASE_ID
npm install --ignore-scripts --omit=dev
node /absolute/private/starforge/forge.mjs doctor --feature postgres
```

Use the existing package declarations. Keep `package.json` and all source files
unchanged so the release continues to match its digest. The dependency tree and
deployment lockfile remain separate from the verified source. The
[merchant distribution guide](../distribution/README.md) provides the original
feature-specific setup and merchant connection instructions.

## Adopt a completed runtime

The original [runtime installer](../distribution/RUNTIME_INSTALL.md) retains the
supplied archive, its original package, the selected dependency profile and its
completed lockfile in one directory. Choose that directory's final location
before preparation; its recorded installation identity includes absolute paths.
Complete the original runtime installation until its inspection reports `READY`.
Place the managed home, retained preparation output and temporary directory
outside that entire runtime directory, including its dependency subtree.

Use the current `starforge installation` CLI to adopt that completed directory:

```sh
STARFORGE_RUNTIME_DIR=/absolute/private/starforge-runtime-v1

npx --no-install starforge installation inspect-runtime "$STARFORGE_RUNTIME_DIR" \
  --expect-manifest PUBLISHED_MANIFEST_SHA256

npx --no-install starforge installation adopt-runtime "$STARFORGE_RUNTIME_DIR" \
  --home "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION" \
  --expect-manifest PUBLISHED_MANIFEST_SHA256
```

The direct Node equivalent uses the current checkout's
`sf46-release/package-cli.mjs adopt-runtime ...`. This is also the adoption
entry point when the original supplied archive predates the installation alias.
The existing home `forge.mjs` remains the launcher for selected releases.

Adoption verifies the original archive and completed runtime through the
original installer, prepares the exact original `package/` contents for SF46,
and binds the runtime identity into `release.json`. The runtime's original
directory remains its source and dependency home. The managed release records
its installation ID, profile ID, profile file hash, lockfile hash, source commit,
source manifest hash and absolute location. These fields contribute to the
managed release digest and release ID.

| Location | Content and ownership |
| --- | --- |
| `RUNTIME/package/package.json` and `RUNTIME/package/source/` | Original supplied package, retained by the runtime installer |
| `RUNTIME/runtime-profile.json` and `RUNTIME/package.json` | Original selected profile and its exact dependency declarations |
| `RUNTIME/package-lock.json` and `RUNTIME/node_modules/` | Completed dependency operation, retained at its recorded runtime location |
| `HOME/releases/ID/package.json` and `HOME/releases/ID/source/` | Exact original package bytes copied by the existing SF46 installer |
| `HOME/releases/ID/release.json` | Verified source release and the immutable runtime selection |
| `HOME/releases/ID/node_modules` | Link to that runtime's dependency directory when the profile selects dependencies |
| `HOME/config/` and `HOME/state/` | Existing merchant configuration and operational data |

A profile with zero selected dependencies is valid: it requires no
`node_modules` link. The original profile still checks its requested Node,
Python, platform and host commands. Dependencies remain owned by the original
runtime installer; use its upgrade workflow to prepare a new runtime directory,
then adopt that completed directory into the same managed home.

The existing SF46 installer performs attachment while holding its original
update lock, after copying and verifying source and before changing the active
release. It creates the expected link or reopens that exact existing link.
Unexpected dependency content produces an error with its path. A failed
attachment leaves the previous active release selected; repeat `adopt-runtime`
with the same runtime and home to resume the verified source installation.

The first completed adoption becomes active. Later adoptions are staged unless
`--activate` is supplied. A different runtime profile or completed lockfile gets
a different managed release identity, even when its source commit is the same.
Use the usual `activate RELEASE_ID` and `rollback` commands to select code and
its retained dependency selection together.

Read the selected release's actual runtime through its copied source imports:

```sh
npx --no-install starforge installation runtime-status \
  --home "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION" --load

# Inspect a staged runtime using the releaseId returned by adopt-runtime.
npx --no-install starforge installation runtime-status \
  --home "$STARFORGE_INSTALLATION" --release RELEASE_ID --load
```

`runtime-status` checks the binding, original profile and lockfile, exact
dependency link, and the original profile against the managed source. `--load`
also asks the original profile inspector to load its selected imports. The
result includes the original runtime paths, selected versions, host inspection
and managed source directory. The existing `doctor --feature NAME` and
`doctor --native` commands continue to use the selected source's original
dependency doctor.

For a retained local preparation, `prepare-runtime RUNTIME_DIRECTORY --out
NEW_DIRECTORY` creates the same source release with its runtime binding. Keep
the original runtime at its recorded location and use the current
`adopt-runtime` command for installation. The current original installer
requires its runtime preparation callback for these bound manifests, so source
selection follows completed attachment.

## Retain a portable prepared release

`prepare` creates a complete SF46 release at a new output path whose parent
directory already exists. Use it when handing the same installable source to
another operator or retaining an exact prepared release for recovery:

```sh
npx --no-install starforge installation prepare "$STARFORGE_PACKAGE_DIR" \
  --out /absolute/deliveries/starforge-prepared \
  --expect-manifest PUBLISHED_MANIFEST_SHA256
```

Retain the returned `id`, `digest`, source manifest hash and `manager` source
identities with that complete directory. The original installer can consume it
directly after transfer:

```sh
node /absolute/deliveries/starforge-prepared/forge.mjs install \
  /absolute/deliveries/starforge-prepared --home /absolute/private/starforge \
  --expect PREPARED_RELEASE_DIGEST
```

The prepared release is retained at the requested path. Temporary preparation is
specific to `installation install`; a cleanup failure is reported as
`temporaryCleanup` alongside the original completed result or original error.

## Application imports

The maintained distribution exposes the same operations for an operator
application:

```js
import { inspectMerchantPackage, prepareMerchantPackage }
  from '@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/installation';
import { installMerchantPackage }
  from '@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/installation/cli';
import { status, activate, rollback, runNative }
  from '@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/installation/product';
import { adoptMerchantRuntime, inspectInstalledRuntime }
  from '@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/installation/runtime';

const selected = await inspectMerchantPackage(packageDirectory, { expectedManifest });
const installed = await installMerchantPackage({
  packageDirectory,
  home: installationDirectory,
  expectedManifest: selected.sourceManifestSha256,
});
const current = await status(installed.home);

const adopted = await adoptMerchantRuntime({
  directory: completedRuntimeDirectory,
  home: installationDirectory,
  expectedManifest: runtimeSourceManifestSha256,
});
const runtime = await inspectInstalledRuntime({
  home: adopted.home,
  releaseId: adopted.releaseId,
  load: true,
});
```

`prepareMerchantPackage({ packageDirectory, output, expectedManifest })` retains
the explicit output; `installMerchantPackage` owns its temporary preparation.
`prepareMerchantRuntime({ directory, output, expectedManifest })` retains a
runtime-bound preparation; `adoptMerchantRuntime` owns its temporary source
preparation and delegates copying, locking and selection to the original
installer. Its returned `runtimeInstallation` includes the actual attachment
and source-based profile inspection.
Importing the CLI module leaves command execution with the caller. `main(args)`
returns the original doctor or native command exit status, and the installed bin
propagates that status to the operating system.

# Source-owned distribution registrations

The pinned Git builder, installed CLI, `doctor` and runtime profiles compose the
base configuration and every direct `contributions/*.json` file through
`specification.mjs`. Each source owns its commands, exported interfaces, runtime
features and original browser asset registrations. The existing base works
without a contributions directory.

## Inspect the installed inventory

```sh
starforge registrations
starforge registrations --source mssql
starforge registrations --command mssql
starforge doctor --feature mssql
```

The first command returns source IDs, original paths and registration counts.
`--source` returns one file's complete declarations. `--command` returns its
effective entrypoint, description and declaring sources. Installed output
includes the original archive commit. Use `--source base` for legacy entries.

Seller providers keep their registrations in [contributions/](contributions/).
Each file combines the provider's existing commands and help, exported interfaces,
runtime declarations and browser contracts. For example,
[postgres.json](contributions/postgres.json) owns the PostgreSQL source and publisher
commands, their interfaces, the original driver manifest and browser entry;
[mssql.json](contributions/mssql.json) does the same for SQL Server.

The directory includes native databases, file and table sources, geographic and
statistical data, scholarly and financial feeds, upstream services, and application
providers. Run `starforge registrations` for the current provider list. A command
can have a different name from its source: `water-quality` belongs to
`wqx-water-quality`, `census-publisher` to `census-acs`, and the original Goldrush
example product to `goldrush`.

Shared seller operations, job delivery, dataset publishing, payment and customer
components keep their existing base registrations. The source-owned files cover
the provider implementations under `sf30-seller-sdk`; independently maintained
buyer and MCP joins use their own current registration owners. A contributor can
locate either kind with `starforge registrations --command NAME`.

When extending a listed provider, edit its existing contribution. Keep command
help beside its command registration; the CLI prints it automatically. Driver
versions stay in the original component package manifest. The base keeps the
shared SF30 component, so these provider files need no duplicate component entry.

## Add one source

Create `contributions/example-source.json` with the following shape, replacing
the illustrated paths with actual maintained files. Omit unused fields.

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.merchant-distribution-contribution.v1",
  "id": "example-source",
  "description": "Example source data products",
  "components": ["stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/example-source"],
  "commands": {
    "example-source": "stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/example-source/cli.mjs"
  },
  "commandDescriptions": {
    "example-source": "Prepare, operate and receive the data product"
  },
  "exports": {
    "./seller/example-source": "./source/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/example-source/index.mjs"
  },
  "runtimePackageManifests": {
    "example-source": "stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/example-source/package.json"
  },
  "browserAssets": [{
    "server": "stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/example-source/workspace/server.mjs",
    "manifest": "stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/example-source/workspace/browser-assets.json"
  }]
}
```

`id` must equal the lowercase filename without `.json`; `base` is reserved.
Use a short, single-line description. A source already inside a maintained
component, such as `sf30-seller-sdk`, does not need another component entry.

| Field | Registration |
| --- | --- |
| `components` | Original source directories included by the builder. |
| `supportFiles` | Explicit additional original files. |
| `excludeFiles` | Explicit omissions under the original builder rules. |
| `commands` | Lowercase command names mapped to original Node `.mjs` entrypoints. |
| `commandDescriptions` | Help for commands declared in the same file. |
| `exports` | Explicit package exports, including ordered conditional exports. |
| `runtimePackageManifests` | Features mapped to original pinned JSON package manifests. |
| `nativePeers` | Original native dependency version and import probe declarations. |
| `featurePeers` | Per-feature dependency declarations and original probes. |
| `browserAssets` | Original server and asset-manifest pairs. |
| `applicationProviders` | Stable provider IDs mapped to original Applications adapter `.mjs` modules. |

The built-in `init`, `run`, `doctor`, `source`, `help` and `registrations` command
names are reserved. Repository source paths must be relative and remain inside
the selected source. Package exports select explicit files under `./source/`.
Command arguments and process lifecycle use the existing CLI.

Keep dependency versions in the original component manifest when available.
`featurePeers` can select its actual exported import subpath. A runtime profile
records the original package-manifest path for a manifest-backed dependency,
and the contribution path for a directly declared dependency. Original version
selection and native-driver preparation still apply.

Browser servers keep using `readBrowserAssets`. Contributions give the existing
collector those same server manifests. [BROWSER_ASSETS.md](BROWSER_ASSETS.md)
defines the URL mapping and original asset closure.

## Applications providers

A product can own its original Applications catalog, command preparation and startup
reader in the same contribution. Add `applicationProviders` with the stable provider
ID and the adapter's original source path. Shared Review/Save, Start/Open/Stop,
private environments, terminals, resource leases and recovery stay in the maintained
runtime. The complete [Applications provider contract](runtime-workspace/APPLICATION_PROVIDERS.md)
contains the native adapter interface, source discovery, exact migration rules and
installed receiving workflow. The existing Databento contribution provides a full
original example. No central catalog or observer branch is required.

## Composition and migration

The base is read first; contribution files are sorted by filename. The directory
is flat so Git and filesystem discovery select the same inventory.

Lists preserve base order and append new values once. Different map definitions
or browser manifests for the same server fail with
`DISTRIBUTION_REGISTRATION_CONFLICT`, naming the key and both source files.
Identical definitions can coexist during migration, with both owners recorded.
Conditional export order is preserved and is part of the compared definition.

Move an existing source's registrations into its contribution without changing
their values, then inspect the effective commands and exports. Other sources
can keep using the base. New source commands generate their own help, so adding
them does not require a central CLI help edit.

## Build and receive the original archive

Use the existing builder with the selected checkout and immutable Git ref:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/path/to/checkout --ref ORIGINAL_COMMIT \
  --out /absolute/private/merchant-package --offline
```

The builder reads and packages the original declaration bytes from that commit.
It preserves source paths, import collection, browser assets and archive rules.
The manifest records `distributionInputs` with Git blobs, lengths and SHA-256
digests, and `distributionContributions` with source IDs and paths. It retains
the existing source file inventory and runtime dependency metadata.

Installed CLI and runtime loading compare the declaration inventory and bytes
with the original manifest. Missing, added or changed contributions are reported
before command selection or runtime preparation. A checkout uses its current
files; package its committed ref for delivery.

# Source-owned Applications providers

Applications discovers its original catalog, preparation logic and startup readers
through the same source contributions used by the maintained merchant distribution.
A product adds its own adapter module and an `applicationProviders` entry; it does
not add another branch to the shared lifecycle or stdout observer.

The runtime still owns Review, Save, Connect, Review Start, Start, Open, Stop and
recovery. Existing application IDs, source/runtime bindings, command arguments,
private environment files, original terminal approvals, resource leases and
retained operation records keep their original meanings. Provider adapters call
the existing native implementation; they do not create a second server or store.

## Inspect and locate a provider

`starforge registrations --source databento` shows the original contribution,
including its provider module. `starforge registrations` includes the effective
provider count and all declaring source files. The Applications state includes a
`providers` inventory with each adapter's path, bytes, SHA-256, declaring
contributions, catalog order and application kind IDs. The existing catalog and
saved applications remain in their original state fields. Each available catalog
entry also carries its stable `providerId`. A missing provider file or module is
listed in `unavailableProviders`, with its declared path and original error;
available tools remain selectable. A catalog integrity error is returned as
`catalogError` with an empty catalog. Saved application and operation history,
Open, Stop and recovery remain readable through their original records.

A checkout reads its selected source files. An installed archive first verifies
the complete contribution inventory against its original manifest, then verifies
each provider module's original bytes before importing it. The builder requires
every declared adapter to be part of its original source selection; its existing
module collector checks the adapter's static imports. Declarations do not execute
provider code during packaging.

## Select one provider for a managed run

Review application and Review Start retain `applicationProvider` with schema
`stellar-forge.runtime-application-provider-binding.v1`, provider `id`,
application `kind`, original `command`, relative source `path`, `bytes`
and `sha256`. The review shows that source beside the original runtime and
command. Saving an application retains the stable provider ID; the next Review
Start captures its then-current exact source. Start compares that reviewed source
before preparing and retaining the original run.

The managed request carries that complete binding. Its ordinary worker follows
the existing request hash, worker lock, QUEUED/RUNNING transition and retained
command launch. Immediately before launch, the registry reads only the selected
provider and checks its declared path, byte length and digest before importing
its module. Its original `matchRequest`, `verifyLaunch`, `prepareChild`
and startup observer still govern the actual command. Missing files in unrelated
providers do not become imports of this selected worker.

`readApplicationProvider({id, kind, expected})` exposes this one-provider
read. `expected` is the complete retained binding, and source readers can
supply the same `sourceRoot` and selected-distribution options used by the
original specification reader. The default complete
`readApplicationProviders()` remains strict. Its explicit
`{allowUnavailable: true}` option is for catalog presentation: only actual
missing-file/module errors can appear in `unavailable`. Conflicting IDs or
kinds, changed installed source, invalid hook contracts and malformed catalog
entries remain errors.

The original `applications.mjs` entry keeps its synchronous
`APPLICATION_CATALOG` export and lifecycle exports for direct callers.
Managed model/worker imports use `applications-core.mjs`, whose lifecycle
has no catalog import at module initialization. Full distribution builds retain
both files through the existing distribution component. A source-selection
recipe that replaces components and previously reached the compatibility entry
only through the model must keep that entry in its existing `supportFiles`
if it exposes it to its consumers.

### Reopen a request retained before provider binding

Continue uses the same application run and operation IDs. It reads that run's
immutable saved application revision, checks its original request/revision
identity, and selects its retained kind. Before preparing the command it writes
one `application-provider.json` receipt in the original operation directory,
binding the provider source to the existing request hash and application
revision. A later restart checks and reuses that same receipt. The original
`request.json`, canonical request hash, arguments and run ID remain intact.

Older direct managed callers without an Applications run retain the original
strict command-matching and ambiguity checks. Ordinary managed commands without
an application ID continue through their original non-application path.

## Add or extend a product

Use the product's existing `distribution/contributions/<id>.json`. Keep its
commands, exports, browser assets and driver declarations unchanged. Add the
original provider module:

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.merchant-distribution-contribution.v1",
  "id": "example-source",
  "description": "Example source data products",
  "applicationProviders": {
    "example-source": "stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/example-source/application-provider.mjs"
  }
}
```

When the source already has a contribution, add that field to it rather than
creating another registration for the same provider. A component can provide more
than one application kind. The existing PostgreSQL and Sheets contributions each
select their separate original authoring and publisher adapters.

The source module default-exports this versioned contract. Replace the example
native imports, command and paths with the actual original product:

```js
import {
  APPLICATION_PROVIDER_SCHEMA,
  observeApplicationStartup,
} from '../distribution/runtime-workspace/application-provider.mjs';
import {
  exampleApplication, prepareExampleApplication, exampleStartup,
} from './managed-application.mjs';

export default {
  schema: APPLICATION_PROVIDER_SCHEMA,
  id: 'example-source',
  order: 1000,
  catalog({ common, field }) {
    return [exampleApplication(common)];
  },
  async prepare(type, settings, context) {
    const original = await prepareExampleApplication(settings, context);
    return {
      args: original.args,
      inputs: original.inputs,
      createDirectories: original.createDirectories ?? [],
      ...(original.resourceKey ? { resourceKey: original.resourceKey } : {}),
    };
  },
  matchRequest(request) {
    return !request.pythonCommand && request.command === 'example-workspace';
  },
  createObserver(request, directory, context) {
    return observeApplicationStartup(request, directory, text => {
      if (!text.startsWith('{"schema":"example.original-startup.v1",')) return null;
      return () => exampleStartup(request, text, directory, context);
    });
  },
};
```

`catalog` receives copies of the original common port/environment fields and the
original `field(name, label, type, required, description)` helper. It returns an
array of ordinary existing catalog entries: stable `id`, original `command`,
`title`, `description`, `terminal`, `fields` and optional `requiredSource`
or original `python` metadata. Field types remain `path`, `text`, `json`,
`boolean` and `port`. The shared UI renders those same entries.

Provider `order` is optional, defaults to 1000 and must be an integer from 0 to
1,000,000. Providers sort by order then ID; multiple entries from one provider
retain their declared order. The migration preserves every original catalog
entry and its original position, including the five installed Python choices and
both event-feed applications.

## Original preparation and validation

`prepare(type, settings, context)` receives normalized original settings.
The context contains the original `root`, `runtimeId`, `runtimeDirectory`,
`inputPath`, `selectedExecutable` and `applicationEnvironment` functions.
It returns `args`, `inputs` and `createDirectories`, plus any original
retained identity fields. Preserve those fields and the original names used by
its native startup reader.

`applicationPreparation(settings, inputPath)` supplies the existing mutable
`args`, `inputs`, `createDirectories`, `path(...)` and `option(...)`
helpers for an adapter that previously prepared its command inline. A thin
adapter over an existing preparer can return its original result directly.

The shared finalizer continues to append the normal port option, prepare the
original terminal executable and read the private environment. It retains
environment hashes and the original terminal flag. Set `appendPort: false`
only when the original preparer already owns that argument, as MPP does.
The original installed Python adapter uses `completeCommand: true` to return
the unchanged full result from its existing Python runtime lifecycle, including
its reviewed Python installation and command binding.

Optional hooks preserve native selection rules:

| Hook | Original operation |
| --- | --- |
| `validateSettings(type, settings)` | Synchronous provider-specific selection checks after the shared field normalization. |
| `checkRuntime(type, settings, runtime, context)` | Required source checks on the selected actual runtime, before command preparation. |
| `resourceKey(type, settings, {hash})` | The original shared workspace or provider resource identity when the default kind/directory identity differs. |
| `runArguments({command, args, requestId})` | Synchronous binding of the original retained run ID into a copied argument list immediately before its managed request is saved. |
| `verifyLaunch(request, operationDirectory)` | Original current-input checks immediately before the managed worker launches its process. |
| `prepareChild(request, operationDirectory, originalArgs, environment)` | An already existing alternative native launch path, such as the installed Python lifecycle. |

A returned `resourceKey` from preparation continues to take precedence over the
fallback identity. Review/Save and Start compare the same current inputs and
source/runtime bindings. The registry does not change those checks or create
another resource-lock directory.

The optional `runArguments` hook runs after Review Start's current inputs and
release checks, with the same operation ID used by the retained managed request.
It returns an array of strings. The worker and Continue reuse the saved arguments;
they do not call this hook again or choose another operation ID. Redis setup uses
it to pass `--setup-operation` to its original connection server so interruption
after workspace creation can reopen that same saved workspace. Ordinary command
preparation and all providers without the hook keep their reviewed arguments.

## Original output readers

`matchRequest` must identify the original managed request without looking at
process output. Most products match their exact command. Shared commands also
match the existing original argv selector: XML and OData use distinct subcommands;
StellarExpert selects its original flag within the dataset command. Installed
Python applications match their existing `pythonCommand` binding. The selector
must return the boolean `true` for an accepted request.

`createObserver` receives the original request, operation directory and process
context. It may delegate a complete existing observer, as Python does, or return
the common `observeApplicationStartup` reader. That reader exposes the same
`write(bytes)` and asynchronous `close()` interface used by the original
managed worker.

The line callback runs synchronously for filtering and multiline assembly.
Return `null` for irrelevant text, an original URL or
`{url, original?, links?}` for an already parsed announcement, or a deferred
function for asynchronous native verification. A deferred function runs only
after preceding candidate announcements have been resolved; an ignored later
announcement never starts another native check. Arrays support original
multiline feeds that complete more than one JSON record in one chunk.

The common reader preserves UTF-8 decoding and original ANSI removal. Its optional
fourth argument `{ lineLimit = 16384 }` selects the original unfinished-line
window (a positive safe integer up to 1 MiB). DuckDB retains 65,536 characters;
WQX, DSpace and Fiscal retain 32,768. Other providers retain the normal 16 KiB
window. Provider-specific assemblers keep their own existing limits. The original feed and wallet assemblers are reused unchanged. Ordinary
log lines are filtered before asynchronous verification is queued.

The first accepted result must point to the original private HTTP loopback
listener. It is retained once in `application-url.json`, with the same
application ID, operation ID, command, observation time and optional original
identity/links. Provider authentication and live listener checks stay in the
original startup function. The registry does not infer a URL from arbitrary
provider payloads or terminal text.

## Source and registration errors

The existing contribution composer coalesces identical provider declarations
during a source migration and records all declaring files. Different paths for
one provider ID produce `DISTRIBUTION_REGISTRATION_CONFLICT` with both owners.
Invalid module paths or non-`.mjs` entries are rejected by the same declaration
validator before source execution.

At runtime:

| Code | Meaning and recovery |
| --- | --- |
| `APPLICATION_PROVIDERS_MISSING` | The selected source does not contain its complete provider declarations. Use the complete original distribution. |
| `APPLICATION_PROVIDER_SOURCE_DUPLICATE` | One module is assigned more than one provider identity. Keep one declaration and stable module ID. |
| `APPLICATION_PROVIDER_SOURCE_CHANGED` | Source changed during reading or differs from the installed manifest. Restore the original archive or select the intended completed release. |
| `APPLICATION_PROVIDER_KIND_DUPLICATE` | Two providers claim the same application kind. Keep that kind with its original owner. |
| `APPLICATION_PROVIDER_KIND_UNKNOWN` | An application kind has no declared provider in this source. Select the release containing its original contribution. |
| `APPLICATION_PROVIDER_COMMAND_UNKNOWN` | A managed application request matches no original provider. Correct the source registration or native selector. |
| `APPLICATION_PROVIDER_COMMAND_AMBIGUOUS` | More than one provider accepts an older unscoped managed request. Use the exact original subcommand or flag selector. |
| `APPLICATION_PROVIDER_BINDING_INVALID` | A run lacks a valid complete provider binding. Reopen its original retained request or review the selected application source. |
| `APPLICATION_PROVIDER_BINDING_CHANGED` / `APPLICATION_PROVIDER_REQUEST_CHANGED` | The selected provider's kind or command differs from the reviewed request. Review the intended source instead of redirecting the saved operation. |
| `APPLICATION_PROVIDER_RECEIVING_CHANGED` / `APPLICATION_PROVIDER_RUN_CHANGED` / `APPLICATION_PROVIDER_REVISION_CHANGED` | A legacy continuation differs from its retained run, immutable application revision or source-selection receipt. Restore those original records and continue the same operation. |
| `APPLICATION_PROVIDER_LOAD_FAILED` | The declared original module or its dependency cannot load. The error includes the provider ID, path and original cause. |

Unknown module fields, missing hooks, duplicate catalog fields and invalid
preparation results are reported explicitly. Non-application managed commands
continue through their existing ordinary command path.

## Receiving and ongoing source changes

Publish the complete adapter, declaration and original source dependencies in one
normal product change. The existing cumulative builder selects that immutable
source; keep its original build and receiving operation. No second package,
dependency installation, UI registry or standalone application launcher is
required.

Applications that reserve several client or coordinator workspaces retain their complete reviewed resource selection through Save, Start and recovery. Their locks are acquired in the original stable order. Older saved runs include any retained `resourceKeys` in the immutable revision comparison before the selected provider is received.

The running Applications host keeps its source inventory for that process.
Receive the following complete release and reopen its original host to discover
new contributions. Existing saved applications retain their original IDs,
runtime/source bindings and histories. Review any actual changed source through
the existing lifecycle before starting it; normal edits within a product's
native workspace remain governed by that original product's identity contract.

The maintained Databento adapter is a complete example:
[provider](providers/databento.mjs), [source-owned registration](../contributions/databento.json),
and [original operator guide](DATABENTO_APPLICATIONS.md). Its provider calls the
same native preparer and authenticated startup reader already operated on the
retained migration workbench. The original producer, customer export and warehouse
receiving do not run again when the source registration is migrated.
